item.title: Corporate Purpose and Socio-Technical Innovation: A Strategic Perspective
item.content:encoded:
Raffaella Montera, Sapienza University of Rome

Mario Tani, University of Naples Federico II

Carlos Rey Peña, UIC Barcelona University

Nicole Steller, ESCP Business School

This special issue examines how corporate purpose and socio-technical systems co-evolve, integrating these concepts within strategic management. As shareholder primacy faces challenges amid systemic fragility and institutional distrust, corporate purpose has become essential for clarifying organizational existence and societal value creation. Digital transformation driven by AI, platforms, and analytics further complicates this landscape, as technical architectures embed values and governance assumptions that shape economic behavior and sustainability outcomes.

The special issue addresses a central strategic tension: the efficiency-driven logic of algorithmic management often conflicts with the long-term, multi-stakeholder commitments required by authentic corporate purpose. The collection welcomes conceptual, empirical, and analytical submissions using diverse methodologies—qualitative, quantitative, mixed-methods, experimental, and case studies—that explore how purpose guides technology deployment and how digital tools operationalize and measure purpose-driven innovation across organizational, board, business model, and ecosystem levels.

Appel publié par Journal of strategy and management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Dynamic capabilities and the strategic enactment of purpose through digital technologies
  • Resource orchestration for purpose-driven AI and data ecosystems
  • The strategic paradox of short-term algorithmic efficiency versus long-term purpose realization
  • Stakeholder strategy, legitimacy, and accountability in purpose-driven socio-technical systems
  • Digital ecosystems as strategic configurations of purposeful identity
  • Boards, leadership, and purpose-driven business models in the digital economy

Timeline

  • January 12, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • February 28, 2027: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Strategy Under Extreme Institutional Shock: Scenario Planning, Foresight, and Strategic Management in the Face of Radical Uncertainty
item.content:encoded:
James Bezjian, The Citadel Military College of South Carolina

Jose Godinez, University of Massachusetts Lowell

Veselina Stoyanova, University of Birmingham

Arpit Sharma, The Citadel Military College of South Carolina

This special issue in the Journal of Strategy and Management examines how organizations respond strategically when major disruptions fundamentally alter the institutional environment and challenge established decision-making frameworks. The focus is on situations where core assumptions, sources of authority, and environmental interpretation become uncertain or contested, requiring organizations to develop new approaches to strategic adaptation and resilience.

The special issue addresses contemporary challenges highlighted by recent global crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic, geopolitical instability, climate disasters, cyber threats, and artificial intelligence advances. By studying how organizations interpret uncertainty, maintain legitimacy, and navigate institutional disruption, the work contributes insights valuable to business leaders, policymakers, and public sector organizations seeking to strengthen resilience amid increasing volatility.

Appel publié par Journal of strategy and management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Extreme institutional shocks and strategy theory
  • High-impact, low-probability events and strategic decision-making
  • Dynamic capabilities under radical novelty and epistemic uncertainty
  • Organizational resilience and adaptation under Knightian uncertainty
  • Strategic responses to pandemics, climate tipping points, and AI discontinuities
  • Institutional legitimacy and re-legitimation following paradigm shocks
  • Managerial sensemaking and cognitive framing under extreme ambiguity
  • Strategy-as-practice during institutional disruption
  • Real options reasoning under Knightian uncertainty
  • Strategic foresight and scenario planning for paradigm-breaking events

Timeline

  • March 30, 2027: Full paper submission deadline
  • January 1, 2029: Publication date of special issue

item.title: Sustainable Strategic Knowledge Management in the Era of AI
item.content:encoded:
Krishna Venkitachalam, Ajman University

Nina Helander, Tampere University

Organizations face increasing volatility and complexity, creating significant knowledge gaps. Sustainable strategic knowledge management has become essential for leveraging intellectual assets—employees' knowledge, skills, and expertise—to achieve financial, social, and environmental objectives.

Artificial intelligence presents opportunities and challenges for knowledge management. AI can enhance decision-making through human-AI synergy and optimize resource use, but organizations must manage AI-generated knowledge responsibly, addressing knowledge overload, duplication, and inefficient transfer. This requires balancing AI capabilities with human expertise while maintaining ethical standards.

This special issue seeks contributions on implementing sustainable strategic knowledge management in AI-enabled environments, including knowledge codification and personalization strategies, managing explicit and tacit knowledge, addressing digital overload, and developing ethical frameworks for AI-integrated knowledge systems.

  • Sustainable organizational knowledge strategies
